narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated an 80.5% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That does not mean failure is certain; it means the model judged it substantially more likely than passing, and the admission decision treated that risk as too high.

The strongest influence was your third-year class-rank decile. You are in the lowest decile, while accepted students average around the sixth decile, so this factor pushed strongly toward a failure prediction. Your first-year class-rank decile was the second most important factor. It was also the lowest decile, again well below the accepted-student average, and it reinforced the same concern about academic performance over time. Your undergraduate GPA was the third most important factor. At 2.80 it is below the 3.23 average for accepted students, but among the top three factors it was the one that worked slightly in favor of passing rather than failing. It was not enough to offset the two class-rank signals.

To proceed, request a human review of your file and ask whether you can submit supplemental evidence, such as an explanation of any extenuating circumstances, evidence of grade improvement, a stronger LSAT retake if feasible, or a concrete bar-exam preparation plan. Also confirm that your academic records are correct and ask about appeal, conditional admission, or deferred admission.
